article.title: NFL EDGE Tuesday Evening Brief
article.dek: Parsons is officially back for Wednesday night, the final injury reports are in, and the evening board has not flipped to Week 12 yet.

items.headline: Parsons is officially back: Packers activate him for Wednesday night
paragraphs: The Packers activated Micah Parsons to the 53-man roster on Tuesday, clearing the last hurdle for his season debut Wednesday night against the Rams at SoFi Stadium.

Parsons tore his ACL and meniscus last December and has missed more than 11 months. He got final clearance from his surgeon on Monday, practiced in full pads on Sunday, and has been limited in practice since. He is officially listed as questionable, and he is expected to play on a snap count as he eases back in.
That settles the question the morning brief left open. One listing still showed him out this morning. He is in now. The Rams will see him Wednesday at 8:00 p.m. ET.
items.takeaway: Parsons is activated, cleared, and expected to make his season debut Wednesday against the Rams, officially questionable and likely on a snap count.

items.headline: Final injury reports: Jacobs unlikely, Walker trending back, Ferguson doubtful
paragraphs: Green Bay running back Josh Jacobs is questionable on the final injury report, but he is still not expected to play Wednesday. He had surgery on his broken right ring finger less than two weeks ago and was limited in all three practices. Coach Matt LaFleur said Sunday and Monday that Jacobs was unlikely to play. Kaleb Johnson leads the backfield if he sits. No Packers player was ruled out on the final report.

Kansas City running back Kenneth Walker III returned to practice Tuesday as a limited participant after missing two games with a groin injury, and he is trending toward a return Thursday night in Buffalo. Dallas tight end Jake Ferguson did not practice again Tuesday and is listed doubtful for Thursday, a step back from the morning, when he was described as out. He has knee and ankle injuries.

Philadelphia cornerback Quinyon Mitchell is questionable with a hamstring injury after not practicing Monday. Running back Saquon Barkley was limited Monday with a neck issue and an illness. Detroit tight end Sam LaPorta was limited Monday with an ankle injury. Chicago cornerback Kyler Gordon and running back Roschon Johnson both did not practice Monday, shoulder and ankle. Kansas City tight end Noah Gray did not practice Monday with a rib injury. Rams defensive end Myles Garrett did not practice Monday with a knee issue and is questionable.

The Rams will also be without two starting offensive linemen Wednesday: guard Steve Avila and center Coleman Shelton are both out with hamstring injuries. Tight end Terrance Ferguson is out for the season and needs ankle surgery. At quarterback, Philadelphia is still without Jalen Hurts, who is on injured reserve and out for the season with blood clots. Joe Milton III starts his third straight game Thursday at Dallas, with Tanner McKee, limited Monday with sore ribs, as the backup.
items.takeaway: Jacobs is questionable but still not expected to play Wednesday. Walker practiced Tuesday and is trending back for Thursday. Ferguson is doubtful, not out. Milton starts again Thursday for Philadelphia with Hurts out for the season.

items.headline: Rain and wind still on for Thursday night in Buffalo; the other games are indoors
paragraphs: Kansas City at Buffalo is still the one outdoor game this week, Thursday at 8:20 p.m. ET at Highmark Stadium. Rain is expected through the day and night, with a 90 percent chance during the day and about 0.72 inches of rain, and an 80 percent chance at night. The high is near 39 degrees, with wind from the east-northeast around 18 mph.

The other three games are under cover. Green Bay at the Rams kicks off Wednesday at 8:00 p.m. ET at SoFi Stadium. Chicago at Detroit kicks off Thursday at 1:00 p.m. ET at Ford Field, a dome. Philadelphia at Dallas kicks off Thursday at 4:30 p.m. ET at AT&T Stadium, a retractable roof.
So the only weather to watch this week is still Buffalo on Thursday night. The forecast can still move before kickoff.
items.takeaway: Thursday night in Buffalo: rain likely all day and night, near 39 degrees, wind around 18 mph from the east-northeast. The Rams-Packers, Bears-Lions and Eagles-Cowboys games are all indoors.

items.headline: The evening board has not flipped to Week 12 yet - no cards tonight
paragraphs: The app still shows Week 11 this evening. The board was read twice after the evening refresh, and both times it showed the morning edition: all 13 Week 11 games, empty market boards, and all three headline cards reading no play. There is no Week 12 line in the app yet, so there is no card to follow tonight.

Saying that plainly matters. The news moved today - Parsons is back, the final reports are in - but the app has not picked any of it up yet. The board refreshes every morning and evening, and the Week 12 lines land when it flips. Check the morning board for the first Week 12 cards.

If your book already has a Week 12 number you like, do not wait on the app to bless it. Type the line and the price into Check and let the app run it back through the model and the evaluator before you bet it. That is what Check is for: a bet or no-bet verdict on your price, not the app's price.
items.takeaway: No Week 12 cards tonight because the evening board still shows Week 11 with empty market boards. Check the morning board for the first Week 12 lines, and use Check on your own book's numbers in the meantime.

items.headline: The board does not know about Parsons yet - your book might
paragraphs: The app still lists the Week 11 quarterbacks and Week 11 numbers. It has no record of Parsons being activated, of Jacobs being unlikely to play, or of Milton starting again Thursday. That is a board that has not refreshed, not a board disagreeing with the news.

When the board and the news disagree like this, the news wins until the board catches up. A line at your book may already have moved on the Parsons news. The app cannot price a move it has not seen, so run your book's line through Check and let it judge the price you can actually bet.

The same goes for Thursday's quarterback. The app has no Week 12 quarterback listed for Philadelphia yet. The reporting says Joe Milton III starts his third straight game with Jalen Hurts out for the season. Take the reporting until the app says otherwise.
items.takeaway: The app has not picked up today's news yet, so a line at your book may already reflect it. Run your book's number through Check rather than waiting for the board to catch up.

items.headline: Key numbers: why 3 and 7 matter more than other numbers
paragraphs: In football, final margins are not spread evenly. Three and seven show up more than any other numbers, because a field goal is worth 3 and a touchdown with the extra point is worth 7. A line that crosses one of those numbers is worth more than a line that crosses any other number.

Here is a clearly labeled hypothetical example. Say a favorite is -3 at -110 in the morning, and by the evening the same favorite is -2.5 at -110. Nothing about the teams changed. But the evening price is better for the favorite backer: a 3-point win pushes at -3 and wins at -2.5. The half point that crosses the 3 is doing real work.
That is why a move from -3 to -2.5 means more than a move from -6 to -5.5, even though both are half a point. Watch which numbers a line crosses, not just how far it moved.
items.takeaway: Three and seven are the most common final margins in football, so a half point that crosses one of them is worth more than a half point anywhere else.

items.headline: No Week 12 lines in the app yet, but the wider market has moved on Packers-Rams
paragraphs: There is no app-tracked movement to report tonight, because the app has no Week 12 lines. The board still shows Week 11 with empty market boards, so NFL EDGE has not verified any Week 12 move against its own numbers.

Outside the app, one odds tracker reports the Rams-Packers line has moved toward Green Bay since it opened, from Rams -3.5 to Rams -2.5, and DraftKings now lists the Rams at -2.5. That move came even with Parsons returning and Jacobs likely out, which points in opposite directions for the two teams.

Treat that as reported movement, not an app verdict. When the board flips to Week 12, this section tracks the openers against the results. Until then, if the -2.5 at your book looks good to you, run it through Check and let the app judge your price.
items.takeaway: No app-tracked Week 12 movement yet, but one tracker reports Rams-Packers moved from -3.5 to -2.5 toward Green Bay, and DraftKings now lists -2.5. That is reported movement, not an app verdict - run your book's number through Check.

items.headline: Wednesday game? Wednesday check.
paragraphs: There is no football tonight. Week 12 starts Wednesday night, Green Bay at the Rams, 8:00 p.m. ET at SoFi Stadium. Thursday brings three games: Chicago at Detroit at 1:00 p.m. ET, Philadelphia at Dallas at 4:30 p.m. ET, and Kansas City at Buffalo at 8:20 p.m. ET.

Inactives land about 90 minutes before each kickoff, and that is when the last injury questions get answered. Parsons and Jacobs stay open until then, and so do Mitchell, Barkley, Gordon, Johnson, Walker and Ferguson.

There is nothing to rush tonight. When the morning board flips to Week 12, look at the cards, and if your book has a number you like, run it through Check first. A good number now beats a hoped-for number later in the week, because waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too.
items.takeaway: No games tonight. Week 12 starts Wednesday night with Green Bay at the Rams, then three Thanksgiving games Thursday. Inactives land about 90 minutes before each kickoff.

evidence.fact: Green Bay activated edge rusher Micah Parsons from the physically unable to perform list to the 53-man roster on Tuesday Nov 24, 2026, setting up his season debut Wednesday vs the Rams at SoFi Stadium. Parsons tore his left ACL and meniscus Dec 14, 2025 vs Denver; received final medical clearance from surgeon Dr. Neal ElAttrache on Monday; practiced in full pads Sunday and was limited Monday and Tuesday. evidence.interpretation: Resolves the morning brief's open question: the listing that still showed Parsons out is superseded by the activation. His return is real but workload-limited.
evidence.app_guidance: Lead with the activation; note the board has not picked it up yet and point readers to Check.
